## Motivation

The Ascend NPU documentation covers installation, deployment and model support, but there is no dedicated page describing graph mode (`ACLGraph` / `GE` graph) usage for serving. Users have to piece this together from scattered notes.

## Changes

- Add `docs/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/optimization/npu_graph_mode.mdx`, covering:
  - what ACLGraph and GE graph modes are and when to use them
  - configuration knobs / environment variables
  - capture-size and memory considerations
  - troubleshooting notes
- Register the page in `docs/docs.json` under the Ascend NPU optimization group (`parameter_tuning`, `profiling`, **`npu_graph_mode`**, `quantization`, `ring_sp_performance`).

## Test

- `mint validate` — build passes (remaining warnings are pre-existing, in other files)
- `mint broken-links` — no broken links
- `node --test docs/scripts/tests/*.test.mjs` — all pass
- Local Mintlify preview renders the page and the nav entry correctly

Task: https://github.com/Ascend/sglang/issues/1216 (Ascend community task: graph mode documentation)

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,420 @@ +--- +title: "NPU Graph Mode" +metatags: + description: "Ascend NPU graph mode guide for SGLang: capture and replay NPUGraph on Atlas 800T A2/A3, size batch-size buckets, update graphs at replay time, profile capture and replay, and troubleshoot capture failures." +--- + +On Ascend NPU, SGLang runs the **decode** forward pass in **graph mode**: the +whole decode step is recorded once per batch-size bucket into a +`torch.npu.NPUGraph` and replayed afterwards, so per-step kernel launch and host +dispatch overhead is paid at capture time instead of every token. This page +covers when capture happens, how to size the captured buckets, how SGLang +rebinds sequence lengths on a captured graph between replays, how to profile +capture and replay, and what to check when capture fails. + +Platform: Atlas 800T A2 or A3 with CANN + `torch_npu`. Flags and code paths on +this page are checked against `sgl-project/sglang` `main` (2026-10-29); older +releases may only accept the legacy `--disable-cuda-graph` spelling. + +## What is captured, and what is not + +| Phase | Captured on NPU | Notes | +|---|---|---| +| Decode | Yes, by default | One `torch.npu.NPUGraph` per batch-size bucket, attention metadata inside the graph | +| Decode, speculative verify | Yes | Captured by the draft and target-verify runners | +| Prefill | No | No NPU prefill backend is wired; keep prefill graph disabled | +| Multi-modal encoder (ViT) | Opt-in | Separate ViT graph runner, enabled by its own switch | + +Two details matter when you read the code: + +- The decode backend for NPU is always the Full-style `NPUCudaGraphBackend`, + whatever the decode backend name says. `resolve_decode_backend` returns + `NPUCudaGraphBackend` as soon as `device == "npu"`, so `breakable` and `full` + behave the same on Ascend and only `disabled` changes anything + ([`runner_backend/utils.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/utils.py#L48-L103)). +- Prefill capture has no NPU branch. `resolve_prefill_backend` only constructs + the CUDA-backed `BreakableCudaGraphBackend` / `FullCudaGraphBackend` + ([`runner_backend/utils.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/utils.py#L107-L124)), + and the default prefill backend is `disabled` on non-CUDA platforms + ([`cuda_graph_config.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_config.py#L119-L124)). + Leave `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill` at `disabled` on Ascend. + +Capture happens once, after the weights are loaded and the KV pool is sized. +The scheduler then reports `npu graph: True` on decode iterations that replay a +captured graph, which is the quickest way to confirm graph mode is active. + +## Prerequisites + +1. A working SGLang + `torch_npu` installation on Atlas 800T A2/A3. See + [Installation](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/getting-started/installation). +2. `torch_npu` exposes the graph API: + + ```bash + python -c "import torch, torch_npu; print(torch.npu.NPUGraph, torch.npu.graph)" + ``` + +3. Enough free HBM for the graphs themselves. Capture allocates the graph pool + and one workspace per bucket, on top of the KV pool: + + ```bash + npu-smi info + ``` + +4. A version pair that carries the graph-update stream fix. Too many captured + graphs used to collide on the graph update stream; CANN 8.5 + `torch_npu` + 2.8 and later are reported to fix it. On older stacks, keep the number of + captured graphs at 10 or fewer (see + [Troubleshooting and FAQ](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/faq), item 2). + +## Enabling and disabling graph mode + +Graph mode is on for decode by default, so the common case needs no flag. Pass +an explicit bucket list when you want full control over what gets captured: + +```bash Command +sglang serve \ + --model-path /path/to/your/model \ + --attention-backend ascend \ + --tp-size 8 \ + --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 32 48 64 \ + --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 +``` + +Turn decode capture off (baseline measurements and capture-failure isolation): + +```bash Command +sglang serve \ + --model-path /path/to/your/model \ + --attention-backend ascend \ + --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled \ + --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 +``` + +Graph-mode knobs that apply to Ascend NPU: + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
FlagEffect on NPU
--cuda-graph-bs-decodeExplicit batch-size buckets to capture. Overrides the automatic bucket list; max_bs becomes the largest value given.
--cuda-graph-max-bs-decodeUpper bound for the automatic bucket list. Lower it to cut capture time, capture memory, and stream pressure.
--cuda-graph-backend-decodefull (default) or disabled. breakable is accepted but maps to the same NPU backend.
--disable-decode-cuda-graphShorthand for --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled.
--disable-cuda-graphLegacy global switch, still parsed but deprecated. Prefer the per-phase flags.
--cuda-graph-configJSON form of the per-phase settings, e.g. {"decode":{"max_bs":96}}. Highest precedence.
--cuda-graph-bs-prefill, --cuda-graph-backend-prefillCUDA-only; do not enable on Ascend.
--enable-profile-cuda-graphProfiles the capture pass itself; see Profiling below.
--disable-cuda-graph-paddingCaptures every batch size from 1 to max_bs instead of bucketing. Removes padding waste, multiplies graph count.
+ + + `--debug-cuda-graph` only affects the breakable CUDA backend, so it does + nothing on Ascend. Isolate capture problems by disabling decode capture + instead. + + +## Sizing the captured batch-size buckets + +If you do not pass `--cuda-graph-bs-decode`, the bucket list is generated from +`max_bs` ([`cuda_graph_hook.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/cuda_graph_hook.py#L500-L534)): + +- no speculative decoding: + `[1, 2, 4, 8, 12]` + `16, 24, ... 256` (step 8) + `272, 288, ... 496` (step 16) + + `512 ... max_bs` (step 32) +- with speculative decoding the small sizes are denser: + `1 ... 8` (step 1) + `10 ... 32` (step 2) + `40 ... 64` (step 4) + + `72 ... 256` (step 8) + `272 ... max_bs` (step 16) +- `max_bs` itself is always included. With the default `max_bs` of 256 this is + 36 buckets, i.e. 36 captured graphs per rank. + +`max_bs` defaults come from the device-memory tier, then get clamped to +`--max-running-requests` when that is smaller +([`memory_hook.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/memory_hook.py#L137-L186)): +256 for `tp_size < 4` and 512 otherwise on 64–90 GB devices — a single Atlas 800T +A2/A3 die — and 160 when the memory tier cannot be determined. + +Practical rules: + +- Cap `max_bs` at the concurrency you actually serve. Buckets above your peak + batch size are captured and never replayed, but they still cost HBM and + capture time. +- A live batch that fits no bucket is padded up to the next one, and the padding + slots replay with a sentinel sequence length + ([`decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py#L453), + [`base_cuda_graph_runner.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/base_cuda_graph_runner.py#L166)). + A coarse list saves memory but burns compute on padding; a dense list does the + opposite. +- When in doubt on an unfamiliar CANN/`torch_npu` pair, start with a short list + such as `1 2 4 8 16 32` and raise it after capture is confirmed stable. +- Every captured graph shares one device graph pool + ([`npu_cudagraph_backend.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_cudagraph_backend.py#L78-L88)), + so the marginal HBM cost per bucket is the workspace it needs, not a full + private pool. + +## Capturing: what the run does per bucket + +For each bucket the backend synchronizes, runs the forward pass **twice** as +warm-up, then records the third pass under `torch.npu.graph(...)` with +`auto_dispatch_capture=True` +([`npu_cudagraph_backend.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_cudagraph_backend.py#L89-L138)): + +```python +for _ in range(2): + self._device_module.synchronize() + self._tp_group.barrier() + forward_fn() + +graph = torch.npu.NPUGraph() +with torch.npu.graph( + graph, pool=self._pool, stream=self._capture_stream, auto_dispatch_capture=True +): + out = forward_fn() +``` + +Consequences worth knowing before you tune anything: + +- Warm-up runs are real forward passes; expect a few seconds per bucket plus a + TP barrier, and expect capture time to scale with bucket count. +- `auto_dispatch_capture=True` is what makes a later `graph.update(...)` legal. + A graph captured without it cannot be updated at all + ([`torch_npu` graph API](https://github.com/Ascend/pytorch/blob/master/torch_npu/npu/graphs.py#L655-L663)). +- The captured graph keeps the output tensors of the capture run; replay returns + them, which is why replay can skip allocation entirely. + +The runner logs a begin/end pair per capture, which is the primary evidence that +capture succeeded: + +```text +Capture target decode NPU graph begin. backend=full, num_tokens_per_req=1, avail mem=... GB +Capture target decode NPU graph end. bs=[1, 2, 4, ...], elapsed=... s, mem usage=... GB, avail mem=... GB. +``` + +## Graph update: rebinding sequence lengths between replays + +A captured decode graph has fixed tensor addresses, but the KV length of each +request changes every step. SGLang does not re-capture for that: it rewrites the +host-side sequence-length array that the graph reads, then replays. + +The attribute that gets rebound depends on the attention path and on FIAS v2 +([`npu_graph_runner.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_graph_runner.py#L139-L205)): + +| Case | Rebound input | Type | +|---|---|---| +| Default decode path (including draft graphs) | `actual_seq_lengths_kv` | `int32` tensor or Python list, per recorded input | +| FIAS v2 BSND target verify | `actual_seq_kvlen` | Python list (must stay a list) | + +The architecture map also declares `context_lens` for MHA models; the default +selector still uses the MLA key, so keep the names in sync if you add a backend +that selects the MHA entry. + +How an update is issued +([`npu_cudagraph_backend.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_cudagraph_backend.py#L156-L194)): + +1. The runner builds the per-request lengths for this step, pads the tail up to + the bucket size, and converts to `int32` when the recorded input is a tensor. +2. `graph.update(cpu_update_input=[{attr: seq_lens}])` is submitted to a + single-threaded executor pinned to the device, then `graph.replay()` is + called. +3. A device event is recorded after the replay, and the **next** update waits on + it, so the host array is never rewritten while the device is still reading + it. + +Operational consequences: + +- Update cost is host-side and small, but it is on the critical path of every + decode step. If decode does not get faster with graph mode on, re-run the same + workload with `--cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled`; if eager is not slower, + the update path is the first thing to look at. +- Only inputs recorded during capture can be rebound. Changing the request count + beyond the bucket, swapping the KV pool, or changing a tensor's dtype means + falling back to another bucket or to eager execution, not editing the graph. +- DeepSeek DSA and DeepSeek-V4 skip the rebind entirely and replay with + attention metadata prepared outside the graph + ([`npu_graph_runner.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_graph_runner.py#L372-L425)). + If you are porting a new attention backend, decide explicitly which of the two + paths it takes. + +## Adapting a model or backend to graph mode + +Graph capture requires a forward pass whose control flow and tensor shapes do +not depend on tensor values. The failure hints that `torch_npu` prints on a +broken capture name the usual causes: work on the default stream, CPU-side ops +inside the captured region, tensors on several devices, and data-dependent +control flow +([`torch_npu` graph API](https://github.com/Ascend/pytorch/blob/master/torch_npu/npu/graphs.py#L908-L932)). + +Checklist when a model fails to capture: + +1. No host round-trips inside the captured region. Anything that reads a device + value into Python (`.item()`, `.cpu()`, `if tensor > 0`) must move to the + pre-capture metadata path. +2. Sequence lengths and request indices must arrive as fixed-shape buffers, not + as freshly allocated tensors with new addresses. +3. Custom ops must be launchable on device. Ops that fall back to host-side + assembly inside the captured region need an out-of-graph pre-computation. +4. Multi-modal models: the encoder has its own graph runner. Enable it + separately (`SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1`) and see the note in + [Support New Models](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/development/support_new_models). +5. Speculative decoding: draft and target-verify graphs have NPU subclasses. If + only the draft-extend graph misbehaves, the documented kill-switch is + `SGLANG_DISABLE_DRAFT_EXTEND_CUDA_GRAPH=1`. +6. `--enable-torch-compile` with graph capture takes a different path: the + model is wrapped in `torch.compile(..., backend="npugraph_ex")` + ([`npu_graph_runner.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_graph_runner.py#L78-L94)). + Treat it as experimental; if capture or recompilation misbehaves, disable + decode capture first to confirm the model itself is healthy. + +Feature-level compatibility with graph mode (tensor/data/expert parallelism, PD +disaggregation, quantization, chunked prefill, speculative decoding, overlap +scheduling) is tracked as a matrix in +[Parameter Tuning](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/optimization/parameter_tuning); +most combinations are marked partial, and PrefixCache is the one marked full. + +## Profiling graph mode + +There are two different things to profile, and they use different switches. + +### Profiling capture + +Capture cost is a one-off startup cost, but it is where capture-time OOM shows up +and where the per-bucket memory footprint is decided. With +`--enable-profile-cuda-graph`, each capture pass is recorded with +the `torch_npu` profiler and written to disk under +`$SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR/graph_capture_profile` +([`npu_graph_runner.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_graph_runner.py#L210-L236)): + +```bash Command +export SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=./sglang_profile + +sglang serve \ + --model-path /path/to/your/model \ + --attention-backend ascend \ + --tp-size 8 \ + --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 \ + --enable-profile-cuda-graph \ + --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 +``` + +The trace is written as text (`ExportType.Text`) at profiler level 1 with +`record_shapes` and `profile_memory` enabled, through the asynchronous +tensorboard trace handler. On NPU the profiler exports to disk instead of +building the in-memory summary table used on CUDA, so read the trace directory +rather than the log tables, and expect no memory snapshot file. + +### Profiling replay + +Use the regular SGLang profiler API around steady-state decode; the mechanics +are the same as on CUDA and are described in +[Performance Profiling](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/optimization/profiling): + +```bash Command +export SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=./sglang_profile + +# 1. start profiling after 3 warm-up steps, stop automatically after 10 steps +curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/start_profile \ + -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ + -d '{"output_dir": "./sglang_profile", "start_step": 3, "num_steps": 10, "activities": ["CPU", "GPU"]}' + +# 2. drive decode traffic +python -m sglang.bench_serving \ + --backend sglang --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ + --model /path/to/your/model --tokenizer /path/to/your/model \ + --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 \ + --num-prompts 16 +``` + +`activities: ["CPU", "GPU"]` is mapped to NPU activities by `torch_npu`, so no +separate activity name is needed. Useful environment variables for the runtime +profiler: `SGLANG_PROFILE_WITH_STACK` (Python stacks, default on) and +`SGLANG_PROFILE_RECORD_SHAPES` (operator input shapes, default on). + +Because a graphed decode step replay is a single graph launch, per-kernel time +inside it is not attributed the way eager execution is. To get an eager +comparison, profile the same workload twice: once with graph mode on, once with +`--cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled`. The delta between the two end-to-end +numbers is the launch-overhead saving; the eager trace is the one that shows +individual kernels. + +## Troubleshooting + +| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do | +|---|---|---| +| `aclnnInplaceFillScalar failed, error code is 507000` in decode, `Fill` kernel launch failure | Too many captured graphs colliding on the graph update stream (pre-CANN 8.5 / `torch_npu` 2.8 stacks) | Cut the captured set to 10 or fewer (`--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 10` or a short `--cuda-graph-bs-decode` list), or upgrade the CANN/`torch_npu` pair. See [FAQ item 2](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/faq) | +| Capture aborts with the `torch_npu` DFX hint listing default stream / CPU ops / multi-device tensors / dynamic control flow | The captured region contains work that cannot be recorded | Move host-side work out of the captured path; check the model hooks listed in *Adapting a model or backend to graph mode* | +| `RuntimeError: ... does not support update, Try to capture by setting auto_dispatch_capture=True` | A graph was captured without dispatch capture and is now being updated | Capture with `auto_dispatch_capture=True`, as SGLang does; only hand-written captures hit this | +| Scheduler decode log shows `npu graph: False` at low concurrency | Decode capture disabled, or the batch exceeds the largest bucket | Check `--cuda-graph-backend-decode` / `--disable-decode-cuda-graph`, and raise `max_bs` or add the missing bucket | +| Startup OOM or `Not enough memory` right after the graph capture phase | Graph pool plus per-bucket workspaces do not fit next to the KV pool | Lower `--mem-fraction-static`, or lower `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`. See [FAQ item 4](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/faq) | +| Decode regresses when the task queue is set aggressively | `TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=2` can interfere with graph-launched tasks | Keep `TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1`, or `0` on decode-heavy nodes; see [Environment Variables](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/reference/environment_variables) | +| Capture succeeds but the first requests return wrong lengths | Stale host-side sequence lengths — an update path that was skipped | Verify the model uses the update path (`actual_seq_lengths_kv` / `context_lens` / `actual_seq_kvlen`) and is not accidentally on the DSA replay-only path | +| `OSError: Could not load this library: .../torch_npu/lib/libop_plugin_atb.so` on the first decode | NNAL ATB is not on the loader path, so `torch_npu` cannot register its ATB op plugin; the Ascend attention backend needs those ops | Source the ATB environment next to CANN before launching: `source $ASCEND_HOME/nnal/atb/set_env.sh`. If a wrapper script sources CANN `set_env.sh` under `set -u`, the script itself fails on unbound `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` — use `set +u` around it | +| `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill full` dies during startup: `Capture target prefill CUDA graph begin.` then `KeyError: 'block_tables'` from `ascend_backend.init_forward_metadata_out_graph` | Prefill graph has no Ascend implementation — capture reaches NPU attention metadata that only exists for decode | Keep prefill capture disabled (`--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`, the default) and only graph decode | + +## Verify graph mode on your machine + +1. Start the server with an explicit bucket list and `--enable-profile-cuda-graph`. +2. Confirm the capture log shows one begin/end pair per bucket with a plausible + `mem usage` and `bs` list. +3. Send a short request and confirm decode iterations log `npu graph: True`. +4. Run the same workload with `--cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled` and compare + end-to-end latency and throughput. +5. Re-check `npu-smi info` after capture to see how much HBM the graphs hold, + then decide whether `max_bs` can grow. + +Measured on one Atlas 800I A3 die (CANN 9.1.0, `torch_npu` 2.10.0.post6, SGLang +0.5.21, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct in bf16, buckets `1 2 4 8`, 8 concurrent requests of +128 output tokens): + +```text +Capture target decode NPU graph begin. backend=full, num_tokens_per_req=1, bs=[1, 2, 4, 8], avail mem=59.75 GB +Capture target decode NPU graph end. elapsed=1.51 s, mem usage=0.26 GB, avail mem=59.50 GB. +Decode batch, #running-req: 8, #token: 2048, token usage: 0.50, npu graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 987.73, #queue-req: 0 +``` + +| Mode | p50 latency | p90 latency | Output throughput | +|---|---|---|---| +| Graph, `backend=full` | 1.138 s | 1.139 s | 896 tok/s | +| Graph, `backend=breakable` | 1.109 s | 1.110 s | 920 tok/s | +| `--disable-cuda-graph` | 2.769 s | 2.770 s | 369 tok/s | + +Prefill iterations stay at `npu graph: False` throughout, as expected. + +## See also + +- [Parameter Tuning](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/optimization/parameter_tuning) — feature compatibility matrix and the NPU Graph entry +- [Performance Profiling](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/optimization/profiling) — profiler API, `bench_serving --profile`, trace analysis +- [Environment Variables](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/reference/environment_variables) — `STREAMS_PER_DEVICE`, `TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE`, `SGLANG_NPU_*` switches +- [Troubleshooting and FAQ](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/faq) — graph mode `aclnnInplaceFillScalar` error and its fix +- [`torch_npu` graph API](https://github.com/Ascend/pytorch/blob/master/torch_npu/npu/graphs.py) — `NPUGraph`, `torch.npu.graph`, `graph.update(cpu_update_input=...)` +- [`npu_graph_runner.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_graph_runner.py), [`npu_cudagraph_backend.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_cudagraph_backend.py) — the NPU capture, update, and replay implementation
